newsitem.title: USA: Feinstein urges hearings on supposed CIA-drug link.
newsitem.headline: Feinstein urges hearings on supposed CIA-drug link.

text.p: Sen. Dianne Feinstein, D-California, urged the Senate on Friday to investigate whether the CIA supported the sale of crack cocaine in U.S. ghettoes to help fund rebels fighting Nicaragua's Marxist government.
Feinstein urged the leaders of the Senate Judiciary and Intelligence committees to hold joint hearings on the issue in the next Congress.
"What is needed is an objective congressional inquiry, which will lay out all the evidence before the public," Feinstein said in a statement.

The San Jose Mercury News published a three-part series in August suggesting that the CIA was involved in financing the Contra rebels, then fighting Nicaragua's Sandinista government, through the smuggling of crack into Los Angeles and other inner-city neighbourhoods in the 1980s.
The Justice Department and the Central Intelligence Agency are investigating the question of CIA involvement.
